6.text: Settlement on the Anadyr began again in the year 1784, but the new

7.text: settlers were not so much Russians as Russianized natives. The village was

8.text: moved to Markova, seven miles distant from the former site.

9.text: The settlement of Nishne-Kolymsk was moved in 1773 to its present site.

10.text: Before that it was situated fifteen miles away, on the so-called Stadukhin

11.text: Channel. This channel was formerly a large branch of the river, but gradually

12.text: it became shallow. The new settlement was founded on the main river,

13.text: opposite the mouths of both Anui Rivers, which enter the Kolyma River almost

14.text: at the same place. The new place had some houses before this transfer. It

15.text: had no strategic advantages, but was excellently chosen for purposes of traffic.

16.text: The old fort was surrounded by palisades. The new one had no palisades,

17.text: though, according to a former tradition, it was also called a “fortress.” Sredne-

18.text: Kolymsk, on the Middle Kolyma, was also fortified in olden times. One small

19.text: wooden tower still stands on the corner of the church courtyard on the hill

20.text: in the middle of the town (see Plate XXXV, Fig. 1).

24.text: TRADE. — One might suppose that some relation still existed between

25.text: the Chukchee and the Russians. Thus, in the year 1779, the Cossack lieutenant,

26.text: Ivan Kobelev, was sent from Gishiginsk to Chukchee Cape.¹ This Kobelev

28.text: Chukchee. In the succeeding half-century he served as the first official inter-

29.text: preter of the Chukchee language. He lived to a very old age, more than.

31.text: Some trade was carried on by barter on the Middle Anadyr, near the

32.text: mouth of the Red River, one of its affluents. There the summer hunting of

33.text: wild reindeer was participated in by all the tribes of the vicinity: and along

34.text: with the Yukaghir and the Chuvantzy, the Reindeer Chukchee also came

35.text: there, and even the Maritime Chukchee in their skin boats. We have infor-

36.text: mation of such a visit of the Chukchee on Aug. 5, 1763.²
